claim: Let \(P_6\) be the path graph on six vertices and let \(P_6\times P_6\) denote the categorical graph product. Then its matching complex satisfies \(\mathsf{M}(P_6\times P_6)\simeq\bigvee^{169}S^{11}\). More precisely, \(P_6\times P_6\) is the disjoint union of two isomorphic connected components \(C\), each with 18 vertices and 25 edges, and \(\mathsf{M}(C)\simeq\bigvee^{13}S^5\); the join decomposition of the matching complex therefore gives the stated wedge of 169 eleven-spheres.
integrity: The graph, all matching faces of one connected component, all Hasse covers, the discrete-Morse matching, its acyclicity, and an independent mod-2 homology computation are reconstructed by the accompanying verifier. No independent audit has been performed.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is only for the single finite parameter pair (6,6); it does not prove the all-parameter conjecture.

title: The matching complex of \(P_6\times P_6\) is \(\bigvee^{169}S^{11}\)
